title: Canonical span translation stream with backpressure and e2e SLO tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a streaming translation layer that converts incoming vendor-specific span payloads into Redwood's canonical span model before forwarding to Tempo/Jaeger backends. The stream must operate with tenant-aware backpressure, per-tenant priority lanes, and a fast path for high-cardinality service traces. This ticket covers the translation pipeline, a token-bucket based backpressure controller, a lightweight schema mapping table with runtime updates, and an end-to-end test harness that validates SLOs under synthetic load.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer converts top-20 vendor attributes (Zipkin, Jaeger, Honeycomb OTLP variants) to Redwood canonical keys with lossless semantic mapping for high-priority fields
Pipeline supports per-tenant token-bucket backpressure and priority lanes; when token pool is exhausted, low-priority spans are shed with a synthetic span indicating reason
End-to-end harness replays 10k traces/min against the pipeline to Tempo and measures 99th percentile ingest latency < 200ms under nominal load
Integration tests include golden trace comparisons and schema drift alerts; failing regression triggers CI gate
Grafana dashboard surfaces per-tenant ingest latency, drop rate, and translation errors; alerts configured for >0.5% drop rate or >250ms p99 latency
notes: Design: prefer stream-first approach (Kafka/streamproc) to avoid buffering bursts in the API tier
Backpressure design trade-off: token-bucket per tenant + global soft-cap. Chosen over strict queue-cap because it better preserves tail latency for VIP tenants
Schema mapping is a small in-memory table backed by a configmap; updates can be applied at runtime via admin API and are versioned
To preserve debuggability, we will emit a synthetic 'redwood.translation.v1' span for any normalized span where a top-level mapping changed semantics
Security: translation does not materialize PII fields; fields flagged as sensitive are dropped and recorded in audit logs per KMS policy
